effects.log: A factor pays you well and asks you to keep listening.

choices.text: Warn the clerks they are overheard

effects.log: They go pale, then generous.

events.text: A drunk immortal jostles you and a cup of century wine goes down the front of a faction lord's robe. The room goes silent. The faction lord looks at the stain, then at you.

effects.log: You kneel. The lord lets the silence go on a long time, then laughs.
You point. It is true, and the drunk is dragged out. You have made an enemy who will live forever.

choices.text: Clean it with a qi-pass before it sets

ok.log: The stain lifts. The lord tips you a stone and asks your name.

fail.log: You make it worse, and the robe was older than you.

events.text: The old keeper sets the keys of the Cloud-Wine House on the counter. "Five hundred years is enough," the keeper says. "The cellar is yours. So are the ghosts in it." Some of the jars down there are older than any living immortal.

choices.text: Take the keys and the ghosts

effects.log: You take them. That night you walk the cellar alone, and something in the dark approves.

choices.text: Ask the keeper to stay a while

effects.log: The keeper stays a decade, teaching you which jars to never open.

events.text: A drifting isle's wine house is failing, and its keeper offers to fly your lantern instead of theirs if you will stand behind its debts. The house has a view straight down through the clouds to the world below.

effects.log: You take it on. A year later it is the busiest house on the drifting road.
You buy it cheap. The old keeper weeps in the doorway as you rehang the sign.
It fails. Another house takes its customers, and they are not yours.

events.text: A minister of the Jade Court wants the oldest jar in your cellar for a banquet where two factions will try to make peace. If the wine is wrong, the peace will be too.

effects.log: The jar is right. The peace holds, for now, and the minister remembers your house.

ok.log: Your blend is spoken of for a century. The peace holds.

fail.log: The blend is wrong. The peace is not your fault, but the wine was.

effects.log: You refuse. Both factions think better of you, a little.

events.text: Your first season on the terraces, you learn that cloud does not want to stay in rows. The terrace hands laugh at your crooked furrows, then show you how to hum to the mist so it settles.

effects.log: By autumn your rows are straight and the mist follows you about like a dog.
Your way works, badly and then well. The hands stop laughing.

events.text: The terrace's cloud-ox will not work for you. It lies in the middle of the terrace, enormous and white, and looks at you as if you were weather.

choices.text: Sit with it until it trusts you

effects.log: It takes the whole spring. By summer it follows you to the edge of the isle and back.
It eats the rice, then works for exactly as long as the rice lasts.

ok.log: It moves. It also remembers.

fail.log: It does not move. You do, quite far.

events.text: Two terrace holders are quarrelling over who owns the rain that falls between their terraces. The rain, meanwhile, falls on neither.

effects.log: You rig a gutter of cloud-silk down the middle. Both sides grumble, and both get wet.
You sell them each the same rain. It is a good season for you.

events.text: A thin year on the terraces: half the spirit rice has come up grey. Three isles depend on your harvest, and the Jade Court's granary officer is asking how much you will send.

choices.text: Send what you promised, and go hungry

effects.log: You send it all. The isles eat; your own hands do not, quite.
You send half and tell the truth. The officer writes it down, without comment.

choices.text: Sell the grey rice as good

effects.log: You sell it as good. Nobody notices for a year.

events.text: An old immortal who holds the next terrace has decided you will inherit it, and has told everyone but you. Their real heir has come up the stairs from below to object.

effects.log: You refuse it. The heir is grateful, and the old immortal never speaks to you again.

choices.text: Take it, and give the heir a place

effects.log: You take it and give the heir a terrace hand's place. Neither of you is happy. Both of you eat.
You take it all. The heir goes back down the stairs.

events.text: Once in three thousand years the peach trees at the edge of your terrace flower. This is the year. Every immortal in the isles finds an excuse to walk past.

effects.log: You open the gate. For one spring your terrace is the most famous place in the Upper Realm.
You charge a stone a visit. They pay, and say it was worth it.
You sit under the blossom alone for a season. It is the quietest you have been since you ascended.

events.text: Your first crossing as a cloud ferryman, a passenger asks how deep the sea of cloud goes. You realise you do not know, and that nobody you have asked does either.

effects.log: It is the right answer. The passenger tips you and does not look over the side again.

choices.text: Ask the old ferrymen that night

effects.log: The oldest one says "it goes down to wherever you came from." You think about that for a long time.

events.text: A chest goes over the side of your skiff in a gust. Its owner, a stern immortal of the Star Sea, says it held their teacher's ashes, and that they will wait on the mooring until you bring it back.

ok.log: You come up out of the cloud with the chest in your arms. The owner bows to you, which immortals of the Star Sea do not do.

fail.log: You come up empty and frozen. The owner waits another hundred years, they say.

effects.log: You pay. Nothing you pay is what it was worth.

choices.text: Say it was the wind's fault

effects.log: It was. That does not help.

events.text: Under a tarp in your skiff you find a child who climbed up from the world below on the back of someone's ascension, and has been hiding on the moorings ever since.

choices.text: Find the child a home on the isles

effects.log: It takes a season of asking. A terrace family takes the child in.

choices.text: Take the child back down the stairs

effects.log: You make the long walk down. The child cries all the way, and waves all the way back up.

choices.text: Hand the child to the wardens

effects.log: The wardens take the child. You do not ask where.

events.text: Two factions want their skiffs to dock first at your moorings. Each has offered you a purse. Each has also hinted at what happens to harbour lords who choose wrong.

effects.log: You keep your own rule. Both factions are angry. Both keep docking.

choices.text: Take both purses and sort it later

effects.log: You take both. Sorting it later is a long, unpleasant century.
You choose openly. One faction is your friend now, and the other is patient.

events.text: The great storm of the century is coming in across the sea of cloud, and forty skiffs are still out. Your moorings are the last safe harbour on the road.

choices.text: Light every lantern and stay on the pier

effects.log: You stand on the pier all night with the lanterns. Thirty-nine skiffs come in.

choices.text: Close the moorings to save the pier

effects.log: You close them. The pier stands. Not everyone does.

events.text: The old ferrymen of the moorings have a song for poling through fog, and they sing it only for those who have crossed a thousand times. Tonight, without a word, they begin it for you.

effects.log: You sing. The fog thins a little, or seems to.
You learn every word. Some day you will sing it to a new ferryman.

events.text: The Lantern Guild house has you counting stones, and a chest of Mid-Grade stones comes up one short every time you count it. The guild elder is watching you count it again.

ok.log: It was never missing: the chest has a false corner. The elder smiles, the first time you have seen it.

fail.log: You cannot find it. The elder writes something down.

choices.text: Make up the stone from your own purse

effects.log: You put in your own stone. The elder knows, and says nothing, and trusts you after.

events.text: A buyer from the Eight Houses wants cloud-silk at half its price, and makes it clear that a factor who wants a future on the isles does not argue with the Eight Houses.

effects.log: You hold it. The buyer leaves. A month later they come back, at your price.
You give it. The guild elder is not pleased.

choices.text: Find a different buyer that afternoon

effects.log: You sell it to someone else by sunset. The Eight Houses notice that too.

events.text: The Lantern Guild elects its master once in a thousand years, and three elders have come to your pavilion at night, separately, each asking what your voice will cost.

effects.log: You promise nothing. Each elder leaves thinking you are with someone else.
You sell it. You are richer, and nobody trusts you now.
You put your own name forward. It is a long century.

events.text: A Celestial Ministry wants to borrow from the Lantern Guild, a great deal, against a promise of favour at the next Court audit. Your seal is the one they need.

effects.log: You lend. The favour comes, years later, at exactly the moment you need it.

choices.text: Lend at a fair rate, no favour

effects.log: You lend fairly. The Ministry is puzzled, then respectful.
You refuse. The Ministry finds another lender, and remembers who said no.

events.text: A convoy carrying a whole season of your trade has vanished in the Isles of Mist. The reavers have sent a single cloud-silk ribbon back, with a price written on it.

effects.log: You pay. The convoy comes back light, and the reavers learn your name.

choices.text: Hire blades to take it back

ok.log: The convoy comes home whole. The reavers find a different road.

fail.log: The blades come home without it.

effects.log: You write it off. The guild elder writes your name down.

events.text: Your first patient at the Lotus Hall is an immortal whose meridians were cracked by a tribulation three thousand years ago. They have been to every healer above the clouds. They expect nothing from you.

choices.text: Listen to the whole story first

effects.log: You listen for a day. You find what the others missed: they were never asked.

ok.log: The needle finds the crack. They weep, which immortals do not do.

fail.log: The needle finds nothing, and hurts.

events.text: The cloud-lotus for the hall's salves blooms for a single night. The master sends you to the pool alone with a basket and a warning: the lotus prefers not to be picked.

effects.log: You ask. It sounds foolish. The lotus opens to you anyway.
You pick fast. The stems bite, and the basket is full.

events.text: A minister of the Jade Court is dying of something nobody will name, and you have been sent for. Three physicians before you were thanked and dismissed. The fourth was never seen again.

choices.text: Cure them and keep the secret

effects.log: You cure them. You never speak of what it was. The minister does not forget.

choices.text: Cure them and tell the Court

effects.log: You tell the Court it was poison. A faction loses its seat. You gain an enemy older than you.
You refuse. Nobody blames you. Nobody calls you again.

events.text: A wing of your hall is full of immortals the last tribulation season nearly killed. There are more of them than beds, and more coming down the cloud road.

choices.text: Open your own pavilion to them

effects.log: Your pavilion becomes a ward. You sleep on the floor for a year.
You treat those who will live. It is right, and it is cold.

choices.text: Charge the factions for their own

effects.log: The factions pay for their wounded. The unbacked wait.

events.text: An old healer of the isles, who taught half the Lotus Halls, comes to you to be treated. It is the first time in ten thousand years that they have let anyone see their hands shake.

effects.log: You treat them like anyone. It is what they wanted.

choices.text: Ask them to teach you while you work

effects.log: They teach you while you treat them. Both of you get better.

events.text: The scroll you are teaching from rewrites its own third line every time you look away. Your students are delighted. You are not.

effects.log: You teach them to read what changed. It is a better lesson than the scroll.

choices.text: Pin it down with a seal

ok.log: The scroll holds still and, you could swear, sulks.

fail.log: The seal slides off. The scroll writes something rude about you.

events.text: One of your students is the heir of a Celestial Ministry, and has never been told no by anyone. Today they tell you, in front of the class, that your reading of the Heavenly Statutes is wrong.

effects.log: They try. They are half right. You tell them so, and they look at you differently.
You correct them. Their parent hears of it before evening.
You agree. The rest of the class stops listening to you.

events.text: Your pavilion's library has drifted three isles over in a storm, and the isle it landed on says that by old law a library that lands is theirs.

choices.text: Argue the old law better than they do

ok.log: You find an older law. The library comes home, slowly, towed by cranes.

fail.log: Their law is older. You visit your library on weekends.

effects.log: You buy back your own books. It is humiliating and fair.

choices.text: Let them keep it, and copy it

effects.log: You spend a century copying it. The copies are better.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries hold their reading of the Heavenly Statutes once a thousand years, and you are asked to set the questions. Three ministers each send a gift, and a question they would like asked.

effects.log: You set your own. The best candidate wins, and the ministers are cold for a century.
You ask them. Three candidates you never met are lifted into the Ministries.
You return them in front of the Court. It is admired, and not forgiven.

events.text: A student you taught in your first century above the clouds comes back a minister, sits at the back of your class, and takes notes like a child.

effects.log: You teach it as always. Afterwards they bow, and say it was the same lesson, and better.

choices.text: Ask them to teach it instead

effects.log: They teach it. You learn something about your own lesson.

events.text: Your first convoy run, the captain gives you the stern of the last skiff and a single instruction: "If anything comes out of the mist behind us, shout. Then fight. In that order."

effects.log: You shout at a cloud shaped like a reaver. Then at a real one. The convoy comes through.
Nothing comes. The captain says you were the calmest stern they have had.

events.text: The trader you are guarding will not say what is in the chest, and it hums when you stand close to it. At night it hums louder.

choices.text: Open it while the trader sleeps

ok.log: It is a caged thunder-spirit. You close the chest and say nothing.

fail.log: The trader wakes as you lift the lid.

effects.log: The trader tells you, and pays you double to forget.

choices.text: Guard it and do not ask

effects.log: You guard it. It is not your business. That is the job.

events.text: The King of the Cloud Road has sent a herald to your convoy house: a toll every season, and your skiffs pass his hidden isles untouched. Every convoy house on the road is waiting to see what you do.

effects.log: You pay. Your convoys pass. The other houses pay too, now that you have.

ok.log: You refuse, and your convoys fight through all season. The King sends a second herald, politer.

fail.log: You refuse, and lose two skiffs before the season ends.

choices.text: Ask the Jade Court for wardens

effects.log: The Court sends wardens, and a bill.

events.text: The heads of the nine convoy houses of the isles meet once a century on a bare rock above the clouds. This time they want one banner over all nine roads, and they are looking at yours.

effects.log: You take it. Every convoy on every road is your problem now.
A council of nine. Slower, fairer, and you sit at its head anyway.
You step back. The isles respect it, and forget you a little.

events.text: A guard of your convoy house fell defending a skiff in the mist. Their family below does not know yet. The house master says the letter is yours to write.

effects.log: You walk the white stairs down and tell them in person. It is the hardest walk you have made.

choices.text: Write it, and send their pay

effects.log: You write it carefully and send everything they were owed, and more.
You send the usual letter. It says nothing true.

events.text: Your first jade warrant is for an immortal who stole a single peach from the Jade Court's orchard three hundred years ago. The warrant has never been cancelled. The thief has a family now.

effects.log: You bring them in. The Court fines them one peach.

choices.text: Let them pay the peach and close it

effects.log: You buy a peach, close the warrant, and keep the story.

events.text: The face on the red-jade warrant in your hand is the face of the warden who posted it. You are fairly sure that is not an accident.

choices.text: Take it to the keeper of warrants

effects.log: The keeper takes it, very calmly, and you are moved to other work for a while.

ok.log: You bring them in. It is a scandal the isles talk of for a century.

fail.log: The warden is stronger than the warrant said.

effects.log: You burn it. Somebody wanted you to.

events.text: The last red-jade warrant the Court has given up on is for an immortal who killed a minister ten thousand years ago and has been free ever since. They have sent you a letter: they know you have their warrant, and they would like to meet.

effects.log: You meet. They tell you why. You still bring them in, or you do not, and you never tell anyone which.

choices.text: Set a trap at the meeting

ok.log: The trap holds. The oldest warrant above the clouds is closed by your hand.

fail.log: They expected the trap.

events.text: Another warrant hunter has been taking the warrants you were about to close, always a day before you. Today they leave a note: "Faster."

effects.log: You race them for a year and win more than you lose.
You hunt together. You close twice as many, and argue about every one.

choices.text: Let them have the small ones

effects.log: You let them. You take the hard ones.

events.text: Your first class on the duelling terrace is twenty young immortals who each think a thousand years of qi makes them unbeatable. They have never been hit by someone who knows how.

effects.log: You put each of them on the ground once, gently. They listen after.
You put them all on the ground at once. Half of them leave. The half who stay are good.
They cannot. That is the lesson.

events.text: A challenger is sitting on your terrace's stair, and has been for nine days, waiting for the master. The master has told you to deal with it.

ok.log: You win. The challenger asks to join the terrace.

fail.log: You lose. The master comes out, and the challenger loses to the master, and you are not forgiven for a decade.

effects.log: You talk for a day. They leave satisfied, without a duel.

events.text: One of the Eight Houses sends its heir to your terrace with a letter: the heir is to be taught, and is never to be struck. The heir reads the letter over your shoulder and grins.

effects.log: You strike them like anyone. The House is furious, and then, a decade later, grateful.
You follow it. The heir learns nothing, and the House pays well.
You send them home. The House remembers.

events.text: A student is knocked off the edge of your terrace in a spar and falls into the sea of cloud. You go after them without thinking.

ok.log: You catch them a mile down. The whole terrace is waiting at the edge when you come back up.

fail.log: You catch them, but the cloud takes its price.

choices.text: Throw a line of qi after them

effects.log: Your qi catches them like a rope. The terrace hauls them in, and the student never spars carelessly again.

events.text: The wine house on this isle will not seat an immortal with no faction, and says so on a board by the door. It is raining, and the next isle is a day away.

effects.log: You sleep under the eaves. In the morning the keeper brings you tea, without a word.
You walk in and sit down. Nobody stops you. Nobody serves you either.
You fly on. The next isle seats anyone.

events.text: A small isle with no faction to protect it is being squeezed by a bigger one for its water. Its elders send a crane to the only immortal nearby who has no faction to offend: you.

ok.log: You stand with them. The bigger isle backs off, and remembers your face.

fail.log: You stand with them and lose, but they keep half their water.

effects.log: You talk both sides to a fair share. Nobody is happy. Everyone drinks.
You keep walking. You are a drifter. That is what the word means.

events.text: Three factions have offered you a rank this century, each a little higher than the last. The fourth has sent a minister in person. Behind you, the drifters you have helped are watching.

effects.log: You refuse. The drifters cheer. The factions find you more useful unbound anyway.
You take it. You are no longer a drifter, and the road knows it.
You ask the faction to seat the unbacked in its halls. It does, a little.

events.text: Around a fire on a bare isle, a dozen drifters with no faction and no house tell stories of the immortals who looked down on them. One of the stories is about you, before you were known.

effects.log: You tell them the rest. They laugh until the fire burns low.
You listen. It is a good story, and only half wrong.

events.text: Your first toll in the mist: a small skiff, an old couple, and a basket of peaches. The lieutenant beside you says the code is the code.

effects.log: You take one peach, and the code is kept. The old couple thank you, confused.
You take it. The lieutenant nods. The peaches are very good.
You wave them through. The lieutenant reports it.

events.text: A Jade Court warship drifts past the hidden isle with its wards dark, close enough to hit with a stone. The chief tells you to keep very still.

effects.log: You keep still. It passes. You breathe again.

choices.text: Mark its hull with a reaver sign

ok.log: You mark it and get back unseen. The crew laughs about it for a year.

fail.log: You are seen. The isle moves that night.

events.text: The chiefs of the hidden isles meet in the mist, and the old King of the Cloud Road is coughing. Everyone is looking at the strongest chief. You realise that is you.

effects.log: You claim it. Every hidden isle raises its cup, and every warden learns your name.
You back the King. Loyalty is rare in the mist, and they do not forget it.

events.text: A captured skiff crew includes an immortal you once knew below, before either of you climbed. They recognise you and say your old name.

effects.log: You let them go. The crew mutters. You do not explain.
You treat them like the others. They do not say your name again.

events.text: Your first commission from the Falling Knife: a name, a garden on an isle, and a night with no moon. The name belongs to an immortal who tends roses.

effects.log: It is done. The roses are not tended any more.

choices.text: Warn them and report a failure

effects.log: You warn them. The Pavilion docks your fee and watches you.

choices.text: Find out who wants them gone

ok.log: You find out. It changes nothing, and everything.

fail.log: You learn nothing, and the Pavilion learns you asked.

events.text: The commission sealed in black jade names a minister of the Jade Court. The fee would buy an isle. The Pavilion's lord says nothing, which means this one cannot be refused.

effects.log: It is done. The Court mourns, and suspects everyone.
You warn them. Now you have a minister who owes you their life, and a Pavilion that wants yours.
You vanish. When you come back, the commission has gone to someone else.

events.text: The knife who has never failed a commission has been given the same name as you. The Pavilion wants to see which of you comes back.

ok.log: You are first. The other knife comes back empty, and looks at you for a long time.

fail.log: They are first. You come back to find your fee already spent.

effects.log: You split it. The Pavilion dislikes that you can.

events.text: Your first feast, you carry the first nectar of the first dawn on a tray to a table where nine gods are pretending not to hate each other. If you spill a single drop, a domain will take offence.

effects.log: Not a drop. A goddess of small winds notices and smiles.
They are flattered. The table calms. The steward makes a note.

events.text: At your table two gods of rival rivers are arguing, a little drunk, about whose world will be flooded next age. Every cup you pour, you learn more about which world.

effects.log: You remember. Somewhere below, a world may yet be warned.

choices.text: Whisper a warning to that world

effects.log: You whisper a dream of rising water. They build higher.

choices.text: Sell it to the Star Market

effects.log: The Star Market pays in faith for news like that.

events.text: The Feast moves to your hall this age, and the seating is yours to set: three pantheons, two wars, and a god who has not spoken to her brother since the world was young.

choices.text: Seat the brother and sister together

ok.log: They speak, for the first time in an age. The Feast is spoken of forever.

fail.log: They do not speak. The table cracks, and so does your reputation.

effects.log: Old law, no offence taken. It is dull and safe.
Your pantheon is pleased. The others remember.

events.text: A pantheon at war asks you to hold a feast for peace in the middle of the fighting. Both sides will come. Both will be armed.

effects.log: You hold it. The peace lasts an age, which for gods is not long, and is everything.
You hold it and remember every word said over the feast.
You refuse. The war goes on. It would have anyway, perhaps.

events.text: Among the offerings carried up for the Feast is a clay cup of rice wine a farmer below poured out for "whatever god is listening." It tastes of smoke and someone's whole year.

effects.log: You hold it and do not drink. You are listening now.

choices.text: Serve it to the highest god at the table

effects.log: The highest god drinks it, and is quiet for a long while.

events.text: Your first harvest in the Harvest Domain, you learn that a sheaf of prayer is heavier than it looks, and that some prayers are thorny.

effects.log: You carry them. Your hands bleed light for a season. The worlds below eat.
You sort them. Slow, sensible, and the reaper beside you calls you cold.

events.text: A world below has sent up nothing this harvest. Its people are too hungry to pray. The granary rule says those who give nothing receive nothing.

effects.log: You send it. The rule is broken, and a world lives.
You follow it. The world is quieter next year.

choices.text: Find a loophole in the rule

ok.log: You find one. Grain goes down as "a loan". Everyone pretends.

fail.log: There is no loophole.

events.text: A blight that eats prayer is in the oldest granary, and it is spreading. To stop it you must burn a whole age of offerings, and the worlds that made them will feel it as a famine of hope.

effects.log: You burn it. The blight dies. Below, a hundred worlds lose faith for a generation.

choices.text: Fight the blight grain by grain

ok.log: You fight it for a century and win. The granary is saved.

fail.log: You fight it and lose half. You saved the rest.

events.text: A very small god of a single orchard comes to the granary to ask for an extra sheaf, because their orchard's farmer has died and nobody prays to them now.

effects.log: You give them one of your own. They hold it like a child.

choices.text: Write them on the granary rolls

effects.log: You enter them in the rolls. They will be fed. They will not be remembered.

events.text: The tide tables you keep for the Sea Domain have one wave too many in a single night, in a world you have never heard of. The chief clerk wants to know why.

effects.log: You go and look. A child below threw a stone into the sea and wished. You leave it in the book.
You erase it. The ledger balances. The child's wish never happened.

events.text: A sea god storms into the Tide Office: their tides were recorded smaller than another sea god's, and they will not be made to look small in the Book.

effects.log: They read them, and are calmed, a little.
You round them up. They leave pleased. The other sea god will notice next age.
You refuse. The sea is rough in three worlds that month.

events.text: A river between the stars has silted up, and the worlds downstream are going dark. Clearing it means asking a dozen domains to move their borders.

ok.log: They move, grumbling. The river runs, and the worlds light up again.

fail.log: Half of them refuse. Half the worlds light.

effects.log: You clear it. Four domains swear revenge.
The Court will see to it, in an age or two.

events.text: In the tide tables you find a line in an old hand: a fisherman who drowned praying to the sea. Nobody answered him. The line has been waiting ten thousand years.

effects.log: You send something down: a quiet sea for his grandchildren's grandchildren.

choices.text: Leave the line as it is

effects.log: You leave it. Some things in the Book are not yours to change.

events.text: Your first day at the Star Market, a god asks you to weigh a measure of luck, and it weighs differently every time you put it on the scales.

choices.text: Weigh it a hundred times and average it

ok.log: The average is fair. The god is impressed, and annoyed.

fail.log: Your average is wrong. The god leaves richer.

effects.log: It came from a sleeping god. You put it down.

events.text: A measure of luck you sold this morning was stolen from a sleeping god, and the god has woken. Their priests are at the market gate asking who sold it.

effects.log: You own up. The god takes the luck back, and something of yours with it.
You point them at the god who sold it to you. That god will not forget.
You pay them in faith to forget you.

events.text: As Assessor of the Star Market you set what a blessing is worth this age. A pantheon has asked you, very politely, to set it low, because it is about to buy a great many.

effects.log: You set it true. The pantheon buys less, and dislikes you more.
You set it low. The pantheon is grateful. A thousand worlds get less luck this age.
You announce it to the whole market. Chaos, and admiration.

events.text: The ghost of a merchant who once prayed to Fortune every day of his life has found his way to the Star Market, and wants to know if any of it worked.

effects.log: You show him. He did better than he thought. He laughs, and fades.
You give him a stall. He is the best trader in the market within an age.

events.text: Your first patient in the Life Domain is a god whose last worshipper has just died. You can feel them thinning under your hands like mist.

effects.log: You hold them to the end. Nobody should fade alone.

choices.text: Find someone below to remember them

effects.log: You send a dream to a child below. A god survives on a single prayer.

events.text: The balm of remembered names is made by writing a god's name on the skin a thousand times. Halfway through, the god asks you to stop: they do not want to be remembered.

effects.log: You stop. They thank you, and fade gently.
You finish. They live, angry and grateful.

events.text: The head of a pantheon is ill with a war that has gone on too long inside them. Their priests want you to cure the god. Their enemies would pay you more not to.

effects.log: You cure them. The war ends, or changes.
You take an age. The war ends without them. Nobody can prove anything.

choices.text: Tell them the cure is to stop the war

effects.log: They hear it. Some gods can.

events.text: A whole world's gods are fading at once, as its people stop believing in anything. The Life Domain sends you with a cart of balm that would treat a dozen of them.

choices.text: Treat the dozen who matter most

effects.log: You treat the dozen. The world keeps a little of its sky.

choices.text: Spend it all on the smallest gods

effects.log: You spend it on the small ones: a well, a doorstep, a kitchen fire. The world stays warm.

choices.text: Ask the world why it stopped

ok.log: You learn why, and carry it back. The Court is troubled.

fail.log: The world has no answer you understand.

events.text: A healer below prays every night to "whatever god keeps the sick," and you realise, reading the prayers, that it is you.

choices.text: Send them a dream of a herb

effects.log: You send a dream. They find the herb. Their village lives.
You listen every night. It is enough, they say, to know someone might.

events.text: Your first page of the Book of Fates: a whole life, from first cry to last breath, and your hand must not shake once. You are halfway down when you recognise the life.

effects.log: You copy it perfectly. Your hand does not shake. Your heart does.
You read it. It is the life of someone you loved below. You copy it later, very carefully.

events.text: A drop of ink falls from your pen onto a page of the Book and becomes, in some world below, a sudden storm.

effects.log: You report it. The keeper sighs and sends a quiet rain to undo it.
You blot it. The storm becomes a cloud. Nobody below notices much.

events.text: Your class of young gods wants to know why the Book is never wrong. One of them has already found a page where it was.

effects.log: You teach it honestly. Some of them will be good gods.

choices.text: Teach that the page is right

effects.log: You teach the old answer. It is safer, and they know it is a lie.

events.text: You keep a whole chapter of the Book now: a world's worth of lives. A god of War wants one line changed, a battle lost instead of won, and says the Court will never notice.

effects.log: You refuse. The god of War waits for an age to be kind to you again.
You change it. A kingdom falls below that should have stood.
The Court notices now.

events.text: Filing old chapters, you find your own page: the life you lived below, the climb, the gates. There is a little space left at the bottom.

effects.log: You leave it. Some things should be written by living them.
You write one line. You never tell anyone what.

events.text: Your first crossing on the Pale Ferry, the master gives you the lantern and says: "If it goes out, do not look at what is in the dark. Just keep rowing."

effects.log: It goes out once. You keep rowing. The souls behind you never know.
You look. You wish you had not. You row faster.

events.text: A soul on your ferry begs to be put off at the wrong shore, a world where someone they love is still alive.

effects.log: You row on. They are quiet the rest of the way.

choices.text: Let them off for a moment

effects.log: You let them see the one they love, from the shore, for a moment. Then you row on.

events.text: Something in the dark between worlds has begun taking souls off the ferries. The master wants an escort to go out past the lanterns and find out what.

ok.log: You find it, and it is only hungry. You feed it something else, and it leaves the ferries alone.

fail.log: You find it, and it finds you first.

effects.log: More light, fewer lost. It is a start.

events.text: Among the souls on tonight's crossing is someone you knew in your life below. They do not recognise you, all light now, with a god's face.

effects.log: You tell them. They laugh, and say they always knew you would end up somewhere strange.
You row them across gently. It is the last thing you can do for them.

events.text: Your first warrant from the Death Domain is for a small god of a forgotten crossroads, who has outlived their last traveller by a thousand years. They are waiting for you with tea.

effects.log: You drink the tea. They tell you about every traveller. Then you carry the warrant.
You carry it. It is kinder quick, they say.

events.text: The god named on your warrant begs, in front of the whole office, for one more age: their world below is about to be born again, and they want to see it.

choices.text: Grant it, on your own word

effects.log: You grant it. If they run, it is your name the Domain will carry.
You carry it. The office is quiet the rest of the day.

events.text: The Death Domain hands you a warrant signed for a god of a great pantheon. The pantheon has made it known that the bearer will not be forgiven.

effects.log: You carry it in daylight. The pantheon does not forgive. The Domain never forgets you either.

ok.log: It is done before the pantheon knows.

fail.log: They know before you arrive.

effects.log: You give it back. Somebody else carries it, and you are never trusted with a great one again.

events.text: In a drawer of the warrant office you find an old warrant with your own name on it, from the life you lived below. It was never carried. Someone signed a note on it: "Not yet."

effects.log: The bearer of the last warrant only smiles.
It does not burn. You put it back.

events.text: Your first drill in the War Domain, a young god tells you that a domain of war has no need for drills: war is what they are. You hand them a practice spear.

effects.log: You beat them. They are a better god of war by evening.

choices.text: Let them beat you, then show them how they did it

effects.log: They win, and you show them why. They come back every day after.

events.text: Two young gods in your drill have started a real war in a small world below to settle a quarrel. Mortals are fighting it for them.

choices.text: Stop the war and punish them

effects.log: You stop it. They spend an age cleaning the world they broke.

choices.text: Make them fight each other instead

effects.log: They fight each other, here, and the world below gets a quiet century.

events.text: An heir of the Elder Lineages comes to your war hall, the first god of their line to learn from someone outside it. Their family has sent a list of things you may not do.

effects.log: You burn it. The heir grins. The family will remember both.
You teach within it. The heir learns what can be learned that way.

events.text: In the War Domain's oldest hall you find drill marks on the floor made by the first god of war, at the first dawn. You can still see where they stumbled.

effects.log: You practise in the marks for a day. You stumble in the same place.
You show them that the first god stumbled. It is the best lesson you ever give.

events.text: A pantheon's temple will not let a god with no pantheon through its gate. Behind you, a small world is praying for rain, and the shortest road runs through the temple.

effects.log: You go round. The rain is late, but it comes.
You walk through. The pantheon remembers.

choices.text: Ask the gatekeeper for a favour

ok.log: The gatekeeper lets you through, quietly.

fail.log: The gatekeeper laughs at you.

events.text: A prayer drifts past addressed to nobody at all, from someone who does not believe in gods. It is the saddest prayer you have ever heard.

effects.log: You answer it, very quietly. They do not believe in you. They feel better anyway.
You let it go. It was not meant for you.

events.text: A small world that prays to you by name has been claimed by a pantheon, which says a masterless god has no right to worship.

ok.log: You defend it. The pantheon withdraws, and tells everyone you are dangerous.

fail.log: You lose, and the world is theirs. It still whispers your name at night.

choices.text: Give it to them, and stay its friend

effects.log: You let it go to them. You visit in dreams.

choices.text: Join a pantheon to keep it

effects.log: You join to keep it. The road is behind you now.

events.text: On the masterless road you meet three other gods of no pantheon. They have made a sort of pantheon of their own, very small, and they would like you to join.

effects.log: You join. It is not a pantheon. It is better.

choices.text: Wish them well and walk on

effects.log: You walk on. You prefer the road.

events.text: Your first raid on the Unlit Sun: a procession of faith from a small temple, guarded by one old god who has clearly never fought.

choices.text: Take half and leave them their way home

effects.log: You take half. The old god thanks you, which is strange.
You take it all. The captain approves.
You let them pass. The captain hears.

events.text: The King of the Unlit Sun has fallen to the Court's host, and the dark shrines are looking for a new one. They are looking at you.

effects.log: You take it. Every pantheon counts its offerings twice now.
You lead the raiders to the Court and ask for pardon. Some are pardoned.

events.text: Among the stolen faith from tonight's raid is a whole village's prayer for a sick child. It glows faintly in the sack.

choices.text: Send it on to where it was going

effects.log: You send it on. The child lives. Nobody on the Unlit Sun knows.
You keep it. It is only faith.

events.text: Your first quiet work for the Silent Hall: a dream, a sleeping god, and an ending the Book of Fates did not write. Inside the dream, the god is a child.

effects.log: It is done, gently. The god wakes less a god, or does not wake.
You leave it. The Hall sees that you did.

events.text: The Silent Hall gives you the dream of a pantheon's head. The fee is enough faith to found a temple. If it is found out, the pantheons will go to war over it.

effects.log: It is done. The pantheons do go to war. The Hall says it was the plan.

choices.text: Warn the sleeper inside the dream

effects.log: You warn them in their sleep. Now a pantheon owes you, and the Hall wants your name back.
You hide in a mortal's dream for an age. It is a very ordinary life. You like it.

events.text: The quiet hand nobody has ever seen is inside the same dream as you, for the same god. You can feel them in the dark, smiling.

ok.log: You find them. They are someone you know. You both pretend you did not.

fail.log: They find you first, and do nothing, which is a message.

effects.log: You leave. The work is theirs, and so is the weight.

events.text: The faction lords who made peace over your wine have quarrelled again, and each has sent word that they will drink only at your house, at separate tables, on the same night.

effects.log: You seat them apart. By midnight they are shouting across the room, which is better than swords.

choices.text: Seat them at the same table

ok.log: They sit together, scowling. By dawn they are drinking from one jar.

fail.log: The table breaks, and so does a jar older than either of them.

effects.log: You close the house. They fight somewhere else.

events.text: Years after the night of the two tables, a quiet immortal comes to your house and pays for a jar for each of the faction lords. "So they will remember where they did not fight," the stranger says.

effects.log: You send them. Both lords come back, separately, and leave large tips.
The stranger smiles. You later learn it was a minister of the Jade Court.

events.text: Someone has been cutting spirit rice from your terrace at night, a single row each time, very neatly. The cloud-ox has seen them and does not seem to mind.

effects.log: You wait. The thief is a fallen immortal from the Under-Cloud Market, starving. You let them work for it instead.

choices.text: Set a ward on the rows

effects.log: The ward catches them. The wardens take them away.

events.text: The fallen immortal you put to work on your terrace has become the best hand you have, and asks, awkwardly, if they may stay for good.

effects.log: They stay. In a century they hold a terrace of their own, and name a row after you.

choices.text: Send them on with a purse

effects.log: You send them on with stones and a letter. They go somewhere better.

events.text: A ferry skiff comes in on its own at dawn with nobody aboard, its lantern still lit. The old ferrymen will not touch it. It is moored at your pier.

choices.text: Pole it out and see where it goes

effects.log: It takes you to a sunken isle, a stair, and a grave with a ferryman's pole on it. You leave the skiff there.
It burns blue. The old ferrymen thank you, and do not say why.

events.text: A house of the Eight wants all your starsteel for a century, and no one else to have any. The price is very good. The other seven houses are watching what you do.

effects.log: You sign. You are rich, and the other seven are patient.
You sell to all of them. None of them loves you. All of them buy.

choices.text: Ask for a seat at their table instead

ok.log: They give you one, at the end. It is still a seat.

fail.log: They laugh, politely, and buy from someone else.

events.text: An immortal of the Demon Realm comes to your hall at night, wounded, asking for help with a hood pulled low. The Lotus Halls do not treat the Demon Realm. Officially.

effects.log: You treat them in the back room. They leave a black pearl on the table.
You turn them away. You do not sleep well.

events.text: Years after you treated the hooded immortal of the Demon Realm, a black fever comes up out of the Under-Cloud, and a messenger brings you its cure, unasked, wrapped in a hood.

choices.text: Use it, and say where it came from

effects.log: The Lotus Halls are shocked, then grateful. The fever ends.
The fever ends. Your hall is famous. Nobody asks.

events.text: Your convoy finds a skiff drifting in the mist with a child asleep in it, a seal of the Eight Houses round the child's neck. The child does not know where they came from.

choices.text: Take the child to the Eight Houses

effects.log: The House is very quiet when it sees the seal. They pay you, and ask you to forget the child's face.

choices.text: Keep the child at the convoy house

effects.log: The child grows up on your skiffs, and asks one day about the seal.

events.text: The fallen immortal on your warrant has an apprentice, a young immortal born above the clouds, who stands in the doorway and will not let you pass.

ok.log: You go through. The apprentice will remember your face for ten thousand years.

fail.log: The apprentice is better than you thought.

ok.log: The master comes out, to spare the apprentice.

fail.log: They will not come out.

effects.log: You leave. The warrant can wait.

events.text: The master of the duelling terrace across the cloud-street challenges you to a public bout. The loser's students go to the winner.

ok.log: You win. Twenty new students cross the cloud-street, and their old master bows to you.

fail.log: You lose. Your own students look at you, and some of them leave.

choices.text: Propose a bout of students instead

effects.log: Your best student wins. The isles say your teaching is better than your sword.
You decline. The cloud-street calls you careful, and not kindly.

events.text: You find, on a bare isle, the grave of a drifter immortal who died alone in the last war of the factions. Someone has been leaving peaches on it.

choices.text: Wait for whoever leaves the peaches

effects.log: It is a minister of the Jade Court, the drifter's friend before the war. You talk all night.

choices.text: Leave a peach of your own

effects.log: You leave one. The next time you pass, there are two.

events.text: A new reaver in your crew has broken the code: they took a skiff of pilgrims and kept the pilgrims for ransom. The crew wants to know what the code is worth.

choices.text: Free the pilgrims, punish the reaver

effects.log: You free them and put the reaver off the isle. The crew follows you harder for it.

choices.text: Take the ransom, warn the reaver

effects.log: You take the ransom. The code is a little weaker now.
The crew decides. You are not sure you like what they decide.

events.text: The Pavilion's lord gives you a mask of white jade with no face on it, worn only by those trusted with names that must never be traced.

effects.log: You wear it. Your commissions are larger now, and darker.

choices.text: Keep it and never wear it

effects.log: You keep it in a drawer. The Pavilion notices.

events.text: A god of a great domain has drunk too much nectar at the Feast and is telling the whole hall a secret of the Heavenly Court.

effects.log: You lead them out. Tomorrow they will thank you, or pretend it never happened.
You let them finish. Every god there now knows something they should not.
They stop mid-sentence, very wet. The hall laughs. The secret is lost in it.

events.text: The Harvest god, oldest of the Green Assembly, walks the granary with you for a whole age without a word, and then says: "You weigh them by hope. Good."

effects.log: "By hunger," the old god says. You think about it for an age.
You keep working. It is the right answer.

events.text: A world below is in its third year of famine, and its prayers have stopped coming. You find out why: it has started praying to the Unlit Sun.

choices.text: Send grain and win it back

effects.log: You send grain. Some of the world comes back to the Harvest.

choices.text: Report it to the Heavenly Court

effects.log: The Court sends a host to the Unlit Sun. The world below is caught between.

events.text: Two sea gods are about to go to war over a reef in a world below. Your tide tables could prove whose it was, if you make them say so.

effects.log: The truth favours neither. They both go home angry, and nobody drowns.
The war ends at once, one-sided. The loser will want you gone for an age.

events.text: A world below is dying, its sun going out. Its last tide is coming in, and the Sea Domain wants it recorded properly.

effects.log: You record every wave. It takes a year. Someone should.
A clerk does it. It is accurate and nothing more.

events.text: A child god of Fortune, very new, has been selling luck at the Star Market for a tenth of its worth, because nobody told them what it was worth.

effects.log: You teach them. In an age they are your fiercest competitor.
You buy it all and sell it on. It is a good age for you.
The elder takes the child aside. The child will not forgive you.

events.text: A pantheon has borrowed a great deal of luck from the Star Market and cannot pay it back. Its head offers you a small domain instead.

effects.log: You take it. A little sea, a few worlds. Yours to keep.
You forgive it. The pantheon owes you more than luck now.
You call it in. The pantheon is shamed, and pays, slowly.

events.text: A god you knew in your first age above, a minor god of a mountain spring, has come to the Life Domain. Their spring below has dried, and so are they.

effects.log: You search a dozen worlds and find a spring with no god. They take it, and live.
You sit with them as they fade. They tell you about the spring. You remember it.

events.text: Someone has been stealing pages from the Book of Fates, a page a year, always lives that ended badly. You find the thief at night: a young god, rewriting the endings.

effects.log: You say nothing. A few lives below end a little better.
You bring them in. The keeper is gentle, and the pages are put back.

choices.text: Teach them to do it properly

ok.log: You teach them which endings can bear changing. Neither of you is caught.

fail.log: You are caught teaching them.

events.text: A clerk of the Book of Fates asks you, quietly, whether the Book writes the lives or only records them. Every clerk asks it eventually.

effects.log: The clerk looks relieved, and goes on copying.
The clerk does not sleep for an age.
The clerk respects that more than either answer.

events.text: The oarsmen of the Pale Ferry have stopped rowing. They want the Death Domain to let them keep a single memory from each soul they carry.

effects.log: You stand with them. The Domain gives way, a little. You are not loved in its halls.

choices.text: Row alone until they come back

effects.log: You row alone for an age. The souls are carried. The oarsmen come back, ashamed.

ok.log: One memory, chosen by the soul. Both sides call it a victory.

fail.log: Nobody agrees.

events.text: A soul of a child is on your ferry, frightened of the dark. The rules say no lantern may be lit for a single soul.

effects.log: You light it. The child stops crying. The master looks the other way.
You tell them a story about a ferry that went somewhere good. It does.

events.text: A god you once carried a warrant for has come back: they cheated their ending, and they have come to thank you for the warning you never gave them.

effects.log: They name someone in the Death Domain. You go very quiet.

ok.log: You carry it, properly this time.

fail.log: They are stronger now.

events.text: The bearer of the last warrant invites you to tea in a room with no door, and asks whether you have ever wanted to stop.

effects.log: They nod. "Everyone does. Keep going." You do.
They look at you for a long time. "Then be careful," they say.

events.text: The god of War who founded your hall challenges you to a bout, as they do every drillmaster once. Nobody has ever won.

ok.log: You do not win. You do not lose either. The god of War laughs for an age.

fail.log: You lose, as everyone does. The god of War approves of how.

effects.log: You fight to learn. You learn more than you wanted.

events.text: One of your young gods of war refuses to fight at all. They say war should be the thing gods prevent. The others laugh at them.

effects.log: You defend them. In an age they are the War Domain's best peacemaker.
They fight, and win, and never forgive you.

events.text: A pantheon sends its herald to the masterless road: a domain of your own, if you will stand with them. The small worlds that pray to you have heard.

effects.log: You refuse. The small worlds pray louder.
You accept. The road is behind you. Your worlds are fed.

choices.text: Ask only for seats for the masterless

effects.log: You ask. The pantheon gives three seats, grudgingly.

events.text: A child below has built a shrine of pebbles to "the god who walks alone." It is the first shrine anyone ever built you.

effects.log: You visit the child in a dream and say thank you. They never forget it.
You tell nobody. It is yours.

events.text: You learn that a raid captain on the Unlit Sun has been whispering to the Heavenly Court for an age. The whole host waits to see what you do.

choices.text: Cast them out into the light

effects.log: You cast them out. The Court gets its spy back, and a message.

choices.text: Use them to feed the Court lies

ok.log: You feed the Court lies for an age. Your raids never meet the host.

fail.log: The Court sees through it.

events.text: A dark shrine on the Unlit Sun is full of offerings nobody came back for: faith stolen ages ago from worlds that no longer exist.

choices.text: Give it to worlds that need it

effects.log: You scatter it over the poorest worlds below. Somewhere, a sky brightens.
You keep it. It is a great deal of faith.

events.text: In a dream you were sent into, you meet the Silent Hall's own lord, asleep. The lord's dream is of being forgiven.

effects.log: You leave. You never tell anyone what you saw.
You forgive them. The Hall is gentler with you after, and you never learn why.

events.text: A mortal below dreams so loudly that your quiet work in a god's dream is broken every night by a child's nightmare.

effects.log: You end it. The child sleeps. Your work waits.
You hide in the noise and finish the work.

events.text: An old regular of the wine house asks for the jar they set aside on their first visit, nine hundred years ago, to be opened on the day they finally stop climbing.

effects.log: You open it together. They say it tastes of every year since.
They say they are tired of being stronger than everyone they love.

events.text: The terrace hands sing at the end of every harvest, a song about the first immortal who tried to farm a cloud and fell through it.

effects.log: You sing it loudest. The hands cheer.
An old hand says yes, and that the immortal was them.

events.text: A child of the moorings wants to pole a skiff alone across the sea of cloud, and has been practising on a plank.

effects.log: You teach them. In a century they are the best ferryman on the road.

choices.text: Let them try the plank first

effects.log: They fall off the plank. They try again.

events.text: In the Lantern Guild's oldest ledger you find a debt owed to a factor who died ten thousand years ago. It was never paid. The ledger says so in fresh ink every morning.

choices.text: Pay it to the factor's grave

effects.log: You pay it at the grave. The ink stops.
You close it. The ink keeps writing, inside.

events.text: Your own tribulation is a century off, and the immortals you have healed come to the Lotus Hall one by one to wish you well.

effects.log: You thank them all. It takes a year.
They do not stop.

events.text: Teaching the Heavenly Statutes, you find an error in them that every minister has repeated for ten thousand years.

effects.log: Your students are thrilled. The Ministries are not.
The Court thanks you and changes nothing.

events.text: The convoy house keeps a wall of names of guards lost in the mist. A new name has to be carved this year.

effects.log: You carve it. Your hands know the letters.

choices.text: Ask the guard's friends to carve it

effects.log: They carve it together.

events.text: The keeper of the jade warrants offers you a desk instead of the road: you would sign warrants instead of carrying them.

effects.log: You sign warrants. You miss the road.
You keep the road. The keeper expected it.

events.text: Your first student, now a master of their own terrace, sends you their best student to finish.

effects.log: You finish them. They are your student's best work, and yours.

choices.text: Send them back with a note

effects.log: Your note says: "Nothing to add." Your student is very proud.

events.text: A young drifter with no faction begs to walk the road with you, so they can learn to be looked down on and not mind.

effects.log: You walk an age together. They mind less.

choices.text: Send them on their own road

effects.log: You tell them every drifter's road is their own.

events.text: The oldest reaver on your isle wants to leave the mist and live on an honest isle before their next tribulation.

choices.text: Let them go with their share

effects.log: You let them go with a full share.

choices.text: Keep them, they know too much

effects.log: They stay. They look at the honest isles every evening.

events.text: Between commissions you keep a garden on a small isle where nobody knows what you do. Someone has found it.

effects.log: It is a child who brings water for the plants. You let them.
You move it. The new one never grows as well.

events.text: The Feast of Domains ends for the age, and the last god at the table is a very small one, still eating, very slowly, to make it last.

effects.log: You sit with them until the end.
You pack them nectar for an age.

events.text: A cat from some world below has wandered into the Harvest granaries and is sleeping on a sheaf of prayer.

effects.log: It stays an age. The granary has no mice. There were never mice.
You carry it home. Its child is overjoyed.

events.text: The chief clerk of the Sea Domain is retiring into the sea itself, as old sea gods do, and asks you to record the last tide they make.

effects.log: You record it. It is a gentle tide.

choices.text: Ask them to stay one more age

effects.log: They laugh, and go.

events.text: A mortal below has prayed for luck every day of a long, unlucky life. Today is their last.

choices.text: Give them a measure of luck now

effects.log: Their last day is the luckiest of their life.
You note it. Fortune does not.

events.text: The master of renewal is fading, and asks you to tend them.

effects.log: You tend them for an age. They live, a little thinner.
You find them a world of healers. They live.

events.text: You copy the last page of a world that has ended. Somebody should read it once before it is shelved.

effects.log: You read it. It was a good world.
You shelve it with the others.

events.text: The oarsmen of the Pale Ferry sing a song for souls who cross alone. Tonight a soul is alone.

effects.log: You sing it. The soul is not alone.
You row in silence. Silence is a kind of company.

events.text: The bearer of the last warrant offers you rest from carrying, for an age, and a room with no door.

effects.log: You rest an age.
You keep carrying. The bearer nods.

events.text: A war in a world below ends because one of your young gods talked it to a close instead of fighting it.

choices.text: Praise them before the War Domain

effects.log: You praise them. The War Domain is confused.
They glow for an age.

events.text: An age passes on the masterless road. You count the small worlds that pray to you now: more than one pantheon expected.

effects.log: You keep walking.

choices.text: Build them a road of their own

effects.log: You join their worlds by a road of light.

events.text: A raider of the Unlit Sun asks to leave the dark and serve a pantheon in the light.

effects.log: You let them go.
They raid one more age for you.

events.text: Between dreams you keep a garden in a mortal's sleep, where nobody can find you. A dreaming child has found it.

effects.log: They play there every night.
You wake them. They will not remember.

events.text: The hill fort that takes you in is three huts and a wall, run by a chief who calls the raiders "the hills' own children" and makes everyone eat together.

effects.log: You eat with them. By winter they are the nearest thing to kin you have here.
You keep apart and watch. You learn who matters.

events.text: Your first toll on the hill road: a farmer's cart with a crying child in it, and a sack of seed for next year.

choices.text: Take a token and let them by

effects.log: You take a single coin. The chief grunts. The farmer remembers.
You take it. Next year a village goes hungry.

events.text: Riders of a kingdom of this world come into the hills with orders to burn every fort. The chief wants to fight. The old ones want to move.

ok.log: The riders turn back. The hills sing about it.

fail.log: The wall falls, and the fort moves anyway.

effects.log: You move it. The riders find ashes and empty hills.

events.text: The forts of every hill in this world send their chiefs to one fire, and the oldest of them holds up the cup that only one may raise.

effects.log: You raise it high and pour it on the fire. Every hill fort in this world is yours.
You pass it back. The hills respect it more than if you had drunk.

events.text: The Lampless Lodge gives you its first name in the dark of a cellar, with no lamp and no list: a name, a town, and a reason you are not told.

effects.log: Nobody answers. That is the answer.
It is done. The Lodge keeps no list, but you will.
You walk away. The Lodge lets you, this once.

events.text: An old member of the Lodge lights a lamp in front of you, against every rule, and says the Lodge was once something else: a house that hid the hunted.

effects.log: They tell you. You leave thinking about it.
You report it. The old member is not seen again.

events.text: The name the Lodge gives you belongs to a king of this world, one of the few kind ones.

effects.log: You warn them. The king owes you a life. The Lodge wants yours.
It is done. The kingdom is unkinder after.
You refuse. Nobody has refused the Lodge in a long time.

events.text: The master of the Lampless Lodge dies without a word, and the Lodge waits in the dark to see who will speak first.

effects.log: You speak. The Lodge is yours.

choices.text: Keep silent and let the Lodge end

effects.log: Nobody speaks. The Lodge ends that night, and nobody misses it.

events.text: Every boat on the great river of this world pays your toll now, and the river folk have started bringing their quarrels to you instead of to the river spirits.

effects.log: You judge fairly. The river folk call you the River Lord and mean it kindly.
You judge for silver. The river is rich and sour.

events.text: The great river rises in a spring flood, and every town along it looks to the River Lord to say which banks to break.

choices.text: Break the banks above your own docks

effects.log: Your docks flood. The towns are saved.

choices.text: Break the banks above the poor towns

effects.log: Your docks are dry. The poor towns are not.

events.text: A prince of a kingdom of this world falls ill, and you are called to the palace with a guard on either side of you.

ok.log: The prince lives, and the kingdom knows your name.

fail.log: The prince lives, barely. The court is cold to you.

effects.log: Half the servants are ill too. You treat them all.

events.text: You find that the queen's illness is no illness, and that the cup it came in was handed to her by her own heir.

effects.log: You tell her. The court is never the same.
You cure her quietly. The heir watches you after.

events.text: The royal child you teach would rather be anywhere else, and has already outlasted three tutors.

effects.log: You teach under the trees. They listen for the first time.

choices.text: Be stricter than the last three

effects.log: You are strict. They learn, and they will not forget it when they rule.

events.text: The royal child asks you, alone, what a good ruler of this world would do about the hill raiders.

choices.text: Tell them to ask why the hills raid

effects.log: They ask. Years later, as ruler, they lower the taxes in the hills.

choices.text: Tell them to burn the forts

effects.log: They remember. Years later, they do.
